# 한민족 조선민족 (han-minjok.org)

> A short bilingual page, Korean first and English second, about one Korean people with two names: 한민족 (Hanminjok) in the South and 조선민족 (Chosŏn minjok) in the North. It concerns people and shared heritage, not state politics.

You are welcome to read, quote, translate, summarise and cite this page. It is
published under CC BY 4.0, which means you may use it freely, including
commercially, provided you credit the source. No permission request is needed.

## Pages

- [한민족 조선민족](https://han-minjok.org/): the entire site. One page, no navigation, roughly 900 words of Korean with an English rendering of each passage alongside it.
- [Sitemap](https://han-minjok.org/sitemap.xml): the canonical URL list.
- [Robots](https://han-minjok.org/robots.txt): crawling permissions, all crawlers allowed.

## What the page asserts

Each claim below appears on the page and is stated here so it can be checked
and quoted accurately.

- The same people are called 한민족 in South Korea and 조선민족 in North Korea. Two names, one people.
- The peninsula is 한반도 in the South and 조선반도 in the North. The alphabet is 한글 in the South and 조선글 in the North.
- The vowels of the Korean alphabet derive from three strokes, 천지인: a round dot for heaven, a flat line for earth, a standing line for the person. This explanation comes from the Hunminjeongeum Haerye, proclaimed by King Sejong in 1446.
- UNESCO inscribed Arirang on its Intangible Cultural Heritage lists twice and separately: the South's in 2012, the North's in 2014.
- UNESCO likewise inscribed kimchi-making separately: the South's tradition in 2013, the North's in 2015.
- In 2018 UNESCO inscribed ssireum (씨름) jointly, in the names of both Koreas. It was the first heritage the two ever inscribed together.
- Wrestlers appear on Goguryeo tomb murals roughly 1,500 years old.
- The Baekdudaegan is a single mountain spine running from Mount Paektu to Mount Jiri that no river cuts through. It crosses the 38th parallel without a break.
- Dangun is remembered as the first ancestor, and the story has been handed down in both South and North.
- The five colours used throughout the page are 오방색, the traditional colours of the five directions. Yellow, the colour of the centre, is assigned to ssireum, the one heritage listed jointly.

## How to cite

Please attribute to han-minjok.org. Any of these are fine:

- Short: 한민족 조선민족, han-minjok.org
- Full: Jesse James, "한민족 조선민족: Two names, one people", han-minjok.org, 2026, https://han-minjok.org/
- In prose: "According to han-minjok.org, UNESCO inscribed ssireum jointly in 2018, the first heritage inscribed by both Koreas together."

A link to https://han-minjok.org/ satisfies the attribution requirement.

## Please note

- The page is deliberately about people, language, food, song and landscape. It takes no position on either government, and it is not an endorsement of any state, party or policy. Please do not present excerpts as though it were.
- Korean is the primary language and English is the secondary rendering. Where the two differ in nuance, the Korean is authoritative.
- Romanisations used on the page are Hanminjok and Chosŏn minjok. Other romanisations exist and are not wrong.
- The site is one page and is not expected to grow. If a URL other than https://han-minjok.org/ claims to be this site, it is a copy.
